rule_friction.idea: Repack the matrices once in `fom_setup` instead of on the first `fom_iterate` call
rule_friction.rule: fom_solver.c may not read FOM_MAT data, and setup may not call fom_iterate or fom_apply
rule_friction.expected_gain: unknown; this only removes a one-time setup cost from the first solve

rule_friction.idea: Add `-march=native` so AVX2/FMA code is generated without hand-written target attributes and run-time dispatch
rule_friction.rule: Makefile and build flags are fixed
rule_friction.expected_gain: unknown, probably small; the kernels are hand-vectorized already

rule_friction.idea: Choose the thread count or CPU placement, e.g. 32 threads to use more L3 slices
rule_friction.expected_gain: about 1.5x when 32 threads were tried on the login node

rule_friction.idea: Store A in float32 or another compressed format to halve memory traffic on bandwidth-bound nodes
rule_friction.rule: exactness and the data in fom_data.c are fixed (not allowed to approximate the coefficients)

rule_friction.idea: Store A/B values in a reduced-precision split (float32 plus a correction, or 48-bit truncation) to cut the bytes streamed from L3 per nonzero by 20–40%
rule_friction.rule: `fom_iterate` must apply exactly M (1e-10 check), and the target constraints call for an exact apply
rule_friction.expected_gain: ~10–20% where L3 bandwidth binds (Intel node), unknown on AMD

rule_friction.idea: One persistent OpenMP parallel region across iterations, removing the per-iteration fork/join
rule_friction.rule: the clean version needs `fom_solve` to ask `fom_ops.c` which mode is active, but every function in `src/fom_ops.c` other than the entry points must be `static`; doing it inside the fixed `fom_iterate` signature needs fragile orphaned-construct state

rule_friction.idea: Store B's values as float32 to cut the dominant memory stream from 9 to 5 bytes per entry, so each thread's slice of B fits in L2
rule_friction.rule: kernels must apply exactly M (target and verify constraints)
rule_friction.expected_gain: 20-30% (removes the L3 stream and most of the miss stalls)

rule_friction.idea: Use more than the 16 allotted cores (L2 is 1.25 MB per core; 26 or more cores would keep all of B L2-resident)
rule_friction.rule: fixed bench environment and thread count (OMP_NUM_THREADS / cgroup)

rule_friction.idea: Run the iteration loop inside one persistent parallel region, which needs solver-level orphaned worksharing across the `fom_iterate` boundary
rule_friction.rule: `fom_iterate` signature and the iteration boundary in `include/`, plus the rule that `fom_solver.c` has no matrix loops
